name: IntuiExtend
author: CIERP Philippe

provenance.from: aminet dev/amos/IntuiExtend20b.lha, held in the corpus at sources/aminet-dev-amos/files/IntuiExtend20b/distribution/extention/. A REAL LIBRARY, not an AMOSTools stub: 23,084 bytes of code hunk behind the table, so this one is `disassembly` rather than `manual`.
provenance.note: The AmigaGuide is vendored beside it and is the extension's own: `@database Intuition AmosExtention.guide @Author CIERP Philippe (c)1995-98 @Version 2.0`, headed "AmosPro IntuitionExtended by CIERP Philippe from AMIGAzette 83." It is in FRENCH, and it indexes the extension by group -- 3d, gadgets, graphics, menus, the PowerPacker library, screens, windows, the system, video and graphic modes, text. The 1.6 build's own $VER is a keyfile line, "To CIERP Philippe, IntuiExtend.lib v1.6", so the release was registered software.
provenance.redistribution: Aminet distribution terms unverified. Kept as a fixture for identification and reference only.

notes: 301 keywords, which makes it the LARGEST third-party table in this registry after OS-DevKit's 1,047 -- larger than AMCAF 1.50's 281. Most names carry a `wb ` prefix and the groups follow the Guide's index: screens (`wb screen open`, `wb screen base`, `wb screen rastport`), windows (`wb wind open`, `wb wind limit`, `wb wind rastport`), exec memory (`alloc mem`, `alloc abs`, `avail mem`, `copy mem`, `set taskpri`), dos segments (`load seg`, `unload seg`, `segment base`), drawing (`wb bevel box`, `wb turtle draw`, `wb paint`, `wb ellipse`, `wb bar`), and a `hard mouse key` that reads the hardware the way CRAFT's `=Hw Mouse Key` does. It shares only three names with anything registered, all with EasyLife. IT IS NOT `int-1.0`, the other `wb `-prefixed extension in this batch: the two share five NAMES and not one ID, and 62 keywords against 301. VERSION 1.6 IS A DIFFERENT TABLE, not an earlier prefix of this one -- of its 294 entries only 45 are still at the id 2.01b uses, so the table was rebuilt between releases and both have to be registered separately or a program tokenised against one detokenises to nonsense under the other. That is the case that put the `renumbered` verdict into src/cli/libcat.ts. Nothing is ported. ONE TABLE ENTRY IS BROKEN IN THE SHIPPED LIBRARY, and it is not a reader bug. Id 2154 comes out as instr $ff00, func $ffff, name "\x00rwb get menu adr", spec "00" -- the only name with a control character anywhere in the registry's 5,326. The bytes settle it. Entry 2136 (`task name`) ends its spec with the $ff at 2153, so the walk resumes at 2154, which is even and needs no alignment skip; AMOS's own Ver_Ech (+Verif.s:5259) advances by exactly the same rule, `tst.b (a0)+ / bpl`, twice and then align. At 2154 the bytes are `ff 00`, then `ff ff 00 72` at 2156, then `wb get menu ad` + $f2 at 2160, `00` at 2175 and the $ff terminator at 2177 -- so the entry the AUTHOR meant starts at 2156: instr absent, func $72 = 114, name `wb get menu adr`, spec "00", ending exactly where the next entry begins at 2178. INTUIEXTEND 1.6 CONFIRMS IT: the same keyword there is `wb get menu adr`, spec "00", instr $ffff, FUNC 114 -- the same routine number, spelled properly. The 2.01b table was rebuilt (only 45 of 1.6's 294 ids survive) and two stray bytes were left in front of this one entry. WHAT IT MEANS FOR A PROGRAM: the keyword is DEAD in 2.01b. Its name cannot be typed, so the tokeniser can never match it, and its instr reads $ff00 = 65280 where the jump table holds 400 routines, so calling it would jump into nothing. Reproduced rather than corrected -- this is what the library does. src/cli/genmanifest.ts escapes the NUL when rendering KEYWORDS.md, because writing it raw made that file binary to git.
